verdict: 18% is reachable on NIFTY 500 only by compounding the risk (1% of current equity instead of 1% of the starting capital). Best: S1bb9f7b0 (Supertrend version, stacked levers, RS ranking, compounding) 19.4% CAGR, Scaa0a5e0 (main version, same) 19.4%. Both draw down 40–46% on NIFTY 500.

No variant passes the acceptance test. Every 18%+ run breaks the −30% drawdown limit on NIFTY 500. The closest, Sa15d9d9c / S1bb9f7b0 (Supertrend, stacked, compounding), hold −21% to −28% on NIFTY 50, NIFTY 100, Midcap 150 and Smallcap 250, but make only 10–16% there.

Without compounding the ceiling is about 13–14%: stacked levers (10 slots, idle cash in a liquid fund at 6.5%, 25-day time stop, RS ranking) give 13.7% on the main version and 12.0% / −20% on the Supertrend version.

A finding about the engine itself: until now every run sized trades at 1% of the starting ₹1 lakh, so as equity grew each trade became a smaller share of the account. That is why recent years looked weak (2019+ hold-out of 4% for S7c315ace). A real trader risks a share of current equity; the compounding results are the more realistic picture of returns and of drawdowns.
Momentum rotation shows 20–43% CAGR, but that is mostly survivorship bias (see F2). Treat it as untested until it can be run on historical index membership.
blocks: A (ATR stop × Supertrend grid): a broad plateau of 7–9% CAGR; wider stops (2.5–3× ATR) cut the drawdown to −17% to −22% at about 7.8%. No cell beats the plain S3f9854aa base by much; the earlier Sd07eb46e result does not carry over to the Supertrend exit.

B (capital at work): idle cash in a liquid fund is the cleanest gain: +1.9 points on the main version, +2.6 on the Supertrend version, with no extra drawdown. Parking idle cash in a NIFTY ETF adds +3 to +5 points but deepens the drawdown to −56%, because that cash falls with the market just when the stops hit. More slots or 1.5% risk add 1–2 points; pyramiding at +2R adds about 1 point; pyramiding at +1R hurts.

C (exits): a 3×ATR daily chandelier trail is ruinous on a monthly system (−5% to −6% CAGR, −75% to −86% drawdown): it is shaken out of nearly every trade (566 trades, median −0.34R). Time stops barely move CAGR but trim the drawdown on the main version (−38% to −36%). Selling half at 2R costs 2.6 points.

D (selection): ranking by 12-month momentum or stock+sector RS adds 0.4–0.9 points on the main version, nothing on the Supertrend version. The top-4-sector filter, near-52-week-high and volume filters all lower CAGR: they throw away good trades.
E (regime sizing): half risk below the 50-DMA, under 50% breadth or with VIX > 25: all cost 0.2–1 point and do not cut the drawdown, the same result as the overnight study.
F1 (second engine): adding the Donchian-55 breakout (2R) to the Supertrend version gives 9.0% / −18.6% from 872 trades; to the main version 12.1% but −44%.

H (compounding): +4 to +8 points on NIFTY 500 for both versions. Drawdowns grow with it: −40% to −59% for the main version, −46% to −56% for the Supertrend version on NIFTY 500, −21% to −28% on the other universes for the stacked Supertrend version. 'w/o top 10' shows −100 for most compounded runs: the 10 largest rupee gains come late, when the account is large, so removing them in rupees is not a fair test for compounding.
rotation: Rotation into today's NIFTY 500 survivors makes 40%; equal weight in the same survivors (no costs) is shown above as the yardstick. Much of the edge is picking stocks that are in the index because they later rallied (RVNL, Suzlon, IRFC, GVT&D gave the largest gains). 89% of the profit comes from 10 trades on NIFTY 200.

The honest benchmark is the published NIFTY 200 Momentum 30 index (built on point-in-time membership), which has historically returned well below these figures. To test rotation properly we need historical constituents; until then it is not a candidate for real money.
risk: Drawdown is the price of 18%. With 1% risk per trade and 8–10 open positions, compounding means a run of stops costs a fixed share of a larger account; in 2018–20 the Supertrend stack lost 46% through many small stop-outs during the mid/small-cap bear market, not one disaster.

Concentration: with compounding, a winner can grow to most of the account (CUPID in the Supertrend stack: ₹15.8 to ₹362, about 65% of equity in 2026; the price data is clean). A position cap (say 20% of equity, trimmed monthly) is a needed rule before real money, and will lower these CAGRs.

Survivorship bias affects every number here, not only rotation: all universes are today's constituents. Swing systems are less exposed than rotation because they hold for weeks with stops, but the absolute CAGRs are still flattering.

What I would trade: the Supertrend version with idle cash in a liquid fund and compounding at 0.75–1% risk (S1bb9f7b0 / Sa15d9d9c family), expecting low-to-mid teens and a drawdown of 25–45%, with the 10%-halve / 15%-pause rule on top. Not 18% with a drawdown I could sit through.
Next tests worth running: a position cap with compounding; drawdown rule (halve/pause) on the compounded stacks; point-in-time constituents for rotation.
